scribeTiers.scribeName: The Day of the Lord As a Thiefe

characters.name: Paul

verses.note: Salutation, rendered in this translation as 'Pavl, and Siluanus, and Timotheus, vnto the Church of the Thessalonians, which is in God the Father, and in the Lord Iesus Christ.'
Gives God thanks always for them, 'remembring your effectuall faith, and diligent loue, and the patience of your hope in our Lord Iesus Christ.'
Recalls that after being 'shamefully entreated at Philippi,' they were 'bolde in our God, to speake vnto you the Gospell of God with much striuing.'
Describes his gentleness among them 'euen as a nource cherisheth her children,' willing to impart not the gospel only 'but also our owne soules, because ye were deare vnto vs.'
'We laboured day and night, because we would not be chargeable vnto any of you, and preached vnto you the Gospel of God.'
'We exhorted you, and comforted, and besought euery one of you (as a father his children).'
Kept from them 'for a season, concerning sight, but not in the heart'; says 'Satan hindered vs' from returning to them, 'I Paul, at least once or twise.'
Could 'no longer forbare,' so remained at Athens alone and sent Timotheus to establish and comfort them, 'lest the tempter had tempted you.'
Comforted by Timotheus bringing 'good tidings of your faith and loue'; asks 'what thankes can wee recompense to God againe for you.'
Closes: 'Brethren, pray for vs... I charge you in the Lord, that this Epistle be read vnto all the brethren the Saintes. The grace of our Lord Iesus Christ be with you, Amen.'

funFacts: Speaks in the plural ('we') for nearly the whole letter, reflecting the joint sending by Paul, Silvanus, and Timotheus named together in this translation's opening verse.

verses.note: Named third in the salutation alongside Paul and Siluanus.
Sent by Paul from Athens as 'our brother and minister of God, and our labour felow in the Gospel of Christ, to stablish you, and to comfort you touching your faith.'
Purpose of his sending restated: 'that I might knowe of your faith, lest the tempter had tempted you in any sort.'
Returns 'from you vnto vs, and brought vs good tidings of your faith and loue,' reporting their good remembrance and desire to see Paul again.

characters.name: Siluanus

verses.note: Named second among the three co-senders of the letter — 'Pavl, and Siluanus, and Timotheus' — this is his only appearance in the book, with no independent action given him in the text.

funFacts: This translation spells the name 'Siluanus' (u/v orthography of the period) — the same companion elsewhere called Silas in Acts, not a different person.

characters.name: Sanctification and Brotherly Loue
characters.purpose: Instructs the church in practical holy living: sexual purity ('know how to possesse his vessell in holines and honour,' abstaining from fornication and the 'lust of concupiscence' as the Gentiles who know not God), warning against defrauding a brother since 'the Lord is auenger of all such thinges,' and continuing in a brotherly loue they are already 'taught of God' to practice, extended to studying quietness, minding one's own business, and working with one's own hands so as to 'behaue your selues honestly towarde them that are without.'

verses.note: 'This is the will of God euen your sanctification, and that ye should abstaine from fornication, that euery one of you should know, how to possesse his vessell in holines and honour.'
'That no man oppresse or defraude his brother in any matter: for the Lord is auenger of all such thinges.'
'Ye are taught of God to loue one another' — brotherly love needs no further instruction from Paul himself.
'Studie to be quiet, and to meddle with your owne busines, and to worke with your owne handes, as we commanded you.'

characters.name: They Which Are A Sleepe
characters.purpose: Addresses grief over believers who have already died, 'that ye sorow not euen as other which haue no hope' — teaching that 'them which sleepe in Iesus, will God bring with him,' that the dead in Christ rise first at the Lord's descent, and that the living remaining will be 'caught vp with them also in the clouds, to meete the Lord in the ayre' — offered explicitly as mutual comfort, 'comfort your selues one another with these wordes,' not doctrine alone.

verses.note: 'I would not, brethren, haue you ignorant concerning them which are a sleepe, that ye sorow not euen as other which haue no hope.'
'If we beleeue that Iesus is dead, and is risen, euen so them which sleepe in Iesus, will God bring with him.'

'The Lord himselfe shall descende from heauen with a shoute... and the dead in Christ shall rise first: Then shall we which liue and remaine, be caught vp with them also in the clouds, to meete the Lord in the ayre: and so shall we euer be with the Lord.'
'Wherefore, comfort your selues one another with these wordes.'

funFacts: This translation's 'them which are a sleepe' / 'them which sleepe in Iesus' phrasing is the same 'caught vp... in the clouds, to meete the Lord in the ayre' passage (4:17) that later English tradition draws the term 'rapture' from — the word itself appears in neither this text nor the KJV.

characters.name: The Day of the Lord As a Thiefe
characters.scribeTier: The Day of the Lord As a Thiefe
characters.purpose: Teaches that the day of the Lord comes suddenly, 'euen as a thiefe in the night,' bringing 'sudden destruction' on those who cry 'Peace, and safetie' as labor pains come upon a woman with child — so believers, as 'children of light, and the children of the day,' must not sleepe as others do but watch and be sober, 'putting on the brest plate of faith and loue, and of the hope of saluation for an helmet.'

verses.note: 'The day of the Lord shall come, euen as a thiefe in the night. For when they shall say, Peace, and safetie, then shall come vpon them sudden destruction, as the trauaile vpon a woman with childe.'
'Ye, brethren, are not in darkenes, that that day shall come on you, as it were a thiefe. Yee are all the children of light, and the children of the day.'
'Let vs not sleepe as do other, but let vs watch and be sober.'
'Let vs which are of the day, be sober, putting on the brest plate of faith and loue, and of the hope of saluation for an helmet.'

characters.name: Quench Not the Spirit
characters.purpose: A rapid closing sequence of instructions for orderly congregational life: acknowledging and holding 'in singular loue' those who labour among them and are over them in the Lord, admonishing 'them that are out of order' while comforting the feeble minded and bearing with the weake, pursuing constant rejoicing, unceasing prayer, and thanksgiving 'in all thinges,' and not quenching the Spirit or despising prophesying while still proving all things and holding fast that which is good.

verses.note: 'Acknowledge them, which labour among you, and are ouer you in the Lord, and admonish you... Bee at peace among your selues.'
'Admonish them that are out of order: comfort ye feeble minded: beare with the weake: be pacient toward all men.'
'Reioyce euermore. Pray continually. In all thinges giue thankes: for this is the will of God in Christ Iesus toward you.'
'Quench not the Spirit. Despise not prophecying. Try all things, and keepe that which is good.'
Closing benediction: 'the very God of peace sanctifie you throughout: and I pray God that your whole spirite and soule and body, may be kept blamelesse vnto the comming of our Lord Iesus Christ.'

genealogyLists.note: Bulk or deliberately-unresolved references, kept out of the character list above.

churches_of_iudea.note: 'Ye are become folowers of the Churches of God, which in Iudea are in Christ Iesus' — a collective example of suffering held up for comparison, not itself indexed as a character or group manager.

those_who_killed_and_persecuted.note: A collective, unnamed polemical reference: 'Who both killed the Lord Iesus and their owne Prophets, and haue persecuted vs away... and forbid vs to preach vnto the Gentiles.' Kept as a bulk reference, not resolved to any individually indexed character.

notes: Read directly from E:/Unity/Clicker_Genesis/Assets/Resources/Verses/Geneva/1_thessalonians_64.json before drafting. The Geneva (1560) text of 1 Thessalonians matches the standard 66-book canon's content and structure verse-for-verse with the KJV rendering of this book (same 5 chapters, same 89 verses, same narrative/doctrinal content) — no real canonical or structural differences were found, only period spelling/orthography (u/v swaps, 'a sleepe' for 'asleep', 'trauaile' for 'travail', etc.) and some archaic word choices ('striuing' for 'contention', 'concupiscence' retained, 'nource' for 'nurse'). Because of that, this draft mirrors the KJV 1Thessalonians.json roster's shape closely by necessity of the source text itself being nearly identical in content — this is a deliberate, evidence-based match, not an uninspected copy: every verse note above quotes the actual Geneva wording read from the source file, not the KJV's phrasing. Only three individuals are named anywhere in the book, all in the salutation at 1:1 ('Pavl, and Siluanus, and Timotheus') — Paul and Timotheus are the only two with independently narrated action (Timotheus's mission to Thessalonica and return, ch. 3), so both got full manager tiers; Siluanus has no independent action beyond the greeting and stays a loyalty-boost submanager under Paul, with a funFact flagging that 'Siluanus' is this translation's spelling of the same companion called Silas in Acts (not a different person). The remaining four tiers are law/theme tiers covering Paul's major teaching blocks (practical sanctification and brotherly love, comfort for the dead/asleep in Christ, the day of the Lord's sudden coming, and closing congregational instructions), since the bulk of the book past chapter 3 is doctrinal/pastoral instruction rather than narrated scenes with other people — consistent with the KJV version of this book being similarly sparse in named individuals. Character/tier ids are suffixed '_geneva_1thess' to keep them distinct from both the existing KJV '_1thessalonians' ids and any future Ethiopian-translation indexing of this same book, per the same book-and-translation-scoped id precedent already used for Jesus across Gospels. Two collective references (2:14's churches of Judea, 2:15-16's unnamed persecutors) are kept as bulk genealogyLists entries rather than invented into individual characters, since the text itself does not differentiate them.
